description: Renovate runs from .github/workflows/renovate.yml as this repository's own job, which is
the self-hosted shape decided on #95. The deciding detail is go mod vendor: only this shape
can run a command in the repository, and a go.mod bump that left vendor/ behind would fail
verify on a tree the bot had made inconsistent.
A proposal arrives WITHOUT a Signed-off-by, deliberately. The decision recorded against Q-1
of XENO-0277 is that a person re-signs each proposal: the DCO's claim is about the right to
submit a change and it stays with a person. An unsigned renovate pull request is therefore
the expected state, and amending it with your own sign-off is the step before merging.
Nothing automerges. Every proposal waits for somebody.
golangci-lint's version is a with: input of its action, and gosec's and govulncheck's are the
@version of a go install line, so each is reached by a regex manager below, as
semantic-release and trivy are. There is no npm manifest in this repository, so
the npm manager is off and semantic-release is reached by a regex instead.
A renovate commit carries no Refs footer. CONTRIBUTING.md puts the issue of the work in
the footer and a dependency bump is the work of no issue; the squash takes the pull
request description anyway, so a footer on the branch commit would not reach main. It
used to read Refs #95, which is the issue that decided this shape and is now closed.
gitleaks, zensical and the image's base are reached by regex managers below for the same
reason the tools above are: the version is a line of a workflow or of the Dockerfile and
no manifest records it. gitleaks is the one whose proposal cannot be complete — renovate
moves GITLEAKS_VERSION and cannot recompute GITLEAKS_SHA256, so the install step fails
the checksum until a person recomputes it. That is loud rather than silent and nothing
automerges, which is the same bargain the supply-chain rows already make.

customManagers.description: semantic-release's version is a with: input of the release action and not a manifest entry, so no ordinary manager sees it.
cyclonedx-gomod's version is a with: input of the CycloneDX action, matched through the action's own name so that a second version: key in the same file is not mistaken for it.
trivy's own version is a with: input of the trivy action, which is pinned separately: the action and the binary it installs move independently and both are rows of docs/supply-chain.md.

golangci-lint's version is a with: input of the golangci-lint action, matched through the action's own name so that another version: key in the same file is not mistaken for it; the action's sha is the github-actions manager's.
govulncheck is installed by go install at a named version of golang.org/x/vuln, which no manifest records; the line is the pin and the Go datasource answers for the module.
gosec is installed by go install at a named version of github.com/securego/gosec/v2, which no manifest records; the line is the pin and the Go datasource answers for the module.

gitleaks is fetched as a release tarball at a version held in an env: block, which no manager sees. The tags carry a v and the variable does not, so extractVersion drops it. The checksum beside it is NOT renovate's to move: a proposal arrives with GITLEAKS_SHA256 stale and the install step's sha256sum -c fails until somebody recomputes it.

zensical builds the documentation site and is pinned on a pip install line in docs.yml, which is not a requirements file, so the pip manager finds nothing. Its fourteen dependencies resolve unpinned at install and are not reachable from here, which docs/supply-chain.md's row already says.

The image's base, as the value of ARG BASE rather than of FROM, which is why the dockerfile manager is not enabled for it. The tag is matched as well as the digest because a digest alone names no stream to follow: docs/supply-chain.md calls this pin debian 13-slim and the reference now says so too.

packageRules.description: A bumped sha is also a row of docs/supply-chain.md, which internal/model/supply_chain_test.go holds against the tree in both directions. Renovate cannot move a Markdown row, so a proposal that touches a pin is a proposal somebody finishes: move the row in the same pull request, or verify stays red on the page rather than on the bump.
One module dependency, vendored. The workflow's postUpgradeTasks re-vendors, so a proposal arrives with vendor/ in step; if that step is ever removed, this manager has to be disabled with it.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The one case that does not wait for the schedule: an advisory arrives without anything in the repository moving, and CONTRIBUTING.md puts the work it names before the next merge rather than after the next feature.
